requires: Follow redirects to the final public response.
Check that a nominal success response does not contain the site's known error or removed-content template.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: HTTP 200 alone is not a healthy-content verdict; soft-error content must not be counted as a passing page state.
limitations: A healthy HTTP state does not prove indexing, ranking, citation or user usefulness.
The verdict is scoped to the probed URL and observation time.

requires: Read the deployed crawler policy rather than only the repository source.
Review current provider documentation for OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot separately.
Confirm the owner's intended search and training policies before evaluating alignment.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: Different policies for search crawling and model-training crawling can be intentional; a difference is not itself a defect.
limitations: Correct crawler policy does not guarantee retrieval or search inclusion.
Provider crawler behavior and documentation can change after the observation.

requires: Nominate only when an AI-readiness or ranking claim appears to be justified mainly by adding llms.txt, ai.txt or another agent-facing file.
Preserve the exact claim and surrounding context for manual review.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: Publishing llms.txt or another machine-readable helper is not the anti-pattern. The problem is treating the file itself as proof of search, citation or AI-readiness outcomes.
limitations: Keyword occurrence cannot establish the claim's meaning.
This detector may never confirm presence or absence; a reviewer must apply the catalog boundary.

requires: Compare visible or structured update dates with evidence of substantive content change.
Nominate repeated date-only refreshes for review rather than declaring them manipulative.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: A recent date can be legitimate when content, evidence, data, policy or availability actually changed. Automated timestamp differences are not enough to confirm fake freshness.
limitations: The detector cannot know the editorial significance of a change from timestamps alone.
Repository history may not match CMS or external data updates.

requires: Compare declared structured-data entity types and claims with visible primary content and actual accessible objects.
Preserve both markup and rendered evidence for review.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: A page may validly describe or expose multiple entity types. Type diversity is not a costume when the declared entities actually exist and match visible content.
limitations: Schema validity and semantic truth are different questions.
An automated parser cannot reliably establish whether the real-world entity or offering exists.

requires: Nominate when implementation or validator success is presented as proof of Search, AI recommendation, citation, traffic or conversion improvement.
Preserve the claimed outcome and the implementation evidence that supposedly proves it.
detectors.falsePositiveBoundary: Showing a green validator result as implementation evidence is correct. The anti-pattern exists only when that result is promoted into an unmeasured growth or visibility outcome.
limitations: The detector cannot infer whether separate owner-side outcome evidence exists elsewhere.
A reviewer must distinguish implementation language from causal or outcome language.
